title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: In 2022-2023, 9 Labour Organisations (LOs) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) have increased their services at Migrant Worker Resource Centers, and MRC-like services in 14 places across the country. The migrant centres are providing a range of services aimed to ensure that workers seeking jobs overseas have access to information and counselling before making decision about migrating. During January 2022- April 2023, LO and CSOs reached and provided services to at least 67,395 beneficiaries (of which 49% are women). These Migrant Centres also provided legal assistance to migrant workers who faced abuses and exploitation during their migration process which led to resolution of cases and total compensation for migrant workers amounting to USD 44,765. Referrals were made based upon requests from migrants through social media to trade unions and CSO to provide direct assistance. The CSOs and Labour Organizations Network for Migrants in Myanmar held monthly networking meeting to update each other about the migration situation in different areas. Quarterly networking meeting on migration into the fishing and seafood processing sectors were held to strengthen coordination and collaboration among CSOs and trade unions. Bi-monthly cross-border cooperation meetings were organized with CSOs and labour organizations in Myanmar and Thailand, including provision of small grants to 15 CSO and trade unions. The Yay Kyi Yar Facebook campaign provided safe migration information to over 1.5 million Myanmar followers across 10 countries. The study "Riding out the Storm: Organizational Resilience of Trade Unions and Civil Society Organizations following the Military Takeover in Myanmar” was launched and received coverage by a dozen national and international media outlets. To date, the campaign has produced 201 original videos and infographics on safe migration, with a total estimated reach of 68,202,962 views online. The ILO, with support from the Government of Australia and the European Union (EU), as well as UN partnership, provided technical support to CSOs and LOs to operate seven Migrant Resource Centres and eight partners to provide services that targeting migrant workers and their families. From 2022-23, ILO, with support from the Government of Australia and the EU, conducted a series of trainings for CSOs and Labour organizations (LO) on mitigation of COVID-19 in agriculture, construction, garment sectors; mental health, safe migration, financial literacy, dissemination of SaverAsia Application, MRC Operations and Monitoring and Evaluation of the programme. With support from the Government of Australia and the EU, 15 worker representatives were supported to join the E-Academy on Labour Migration Course in December 2022. The ILO, with support from the Government of Australia, supported the networking meetings of CSOs and LOs Network to provide better services and strengthened coordination and collaboration. The ILO, with support from the EU, collaborated with IOM to organize cross-border cooperation meetings with CSOs, trade unions and international organizations working on safe migration in Myanmar and Thailand. The ILO, with support from the EU, launched new informational materials on safe migration, labour rights, and occupational safety and health in the fishing and seafood processing sectors, with 10,000 copies printed for distribution by MRCs. The ILO, with support from the EU, coordinated with CSOs and LOs to organise social media and public information campaign promoting C189, C190. The campaign had 31,000 views on the Yay Kyi Yar page. The ILO, with support from the European Union, funded BBC Media Action to implement the Yay Kyi Yar Facebook campaign.
